content.text: {"headline":"Approve P3 (combined no-overtime response, ₹252), but involve the duty manager now: no available plan gets close to the 80% target for 13:00-15:00.","why":"The surge is caused by the UPI switch outage (P1 incident INC-20261006-6998). Payments calls hit 213 against 111.9 forecast, and upi_payment_failed calls are running 2.56x normal. Staffing is at plan (42 of 43) and handle time is below forecast, so this is a demand problem, not a staffing one. With overtime ruled out today, P3 combines every remaining lever: 45-minute break delays on both queues from 14:00, an IVR outage message, IVR callback and 20% chat deflection on payments. It is predicted to reach 46.5% service level for 13:00-15:00 (payments 35.3%, general 67.6%) with 13.6% abandons, against 46.2% and 13.8% if we do nothing. That is the best result of any compliant plan, but only marginally better. Escalation is flagged because 46% is below the 70% escalation line (ESC-02). The duty manager should be involved to consider options outside today's constraints, such as releasing overtime budget or extra outage handling.","trade_offs":["P0 (no action, ₹0) predicts 46.2%. P3 adds only about 0.3 points for ₹252, so the gain is small.","P1 (free break shift plus callback) predicts 45.5% and lowers general to 63.7%. It costs nothing but performs slightly worse.","P2 (₹168) and R1/R2 (₹324/₹372) all predict 45.9-46.1% and cost the same or more for no improvement.","P3 delays general-queue breaks too, yet general still improves to 67.6%, so there is no added risk to the other queue. Payments stays at about 35% under every plan."],"watch":"Watch payments arrivals and abandons each interval, and the INC-20261006-6998 status. If the UPI switch recovers, volume should fall and break delays can be relaxed. If the outage runs past 15:00, extended deflection (as in R1/R2) and duty-manager decisions on extra capacity will be needed."}
